label: Buddhism (secular / modernist reading)
summary: A Western-modernist reading (Batchelor; the mindfulness movement) of the Buddha's core diagnosis: suffering arises from craving and clinging and can be released through ethical living, meditation, and insight into impermanence and non-self — taken as a pragmatic, testable path for this life, while bracketing or naturalizing rebirth, cross-life karma, and cosmology.
variants: The secular/traditional split is the headline: traditional Theravada, Mahayana, and Vajrayana affirm literal rebirth, cross-life karmic causation, and liberation from the rebirth cycle (supernaturalist by Western categories, though non-theist), and traditionalists argue that removing rebirth guts Right View. The clinical mindfulness movement is a further de-ethicized extraction both camps criticize. Positions below follow the secular reading; progress is omitted as orthogonal (liberation is inner transformation, not material progress).

positions.summary: Experiential-pragmatic ('come and see'): first-person contemplative investigation, fallibilist in the secular version and in dialogue with psychology and neuroscience.
Deep insight into mind and suffering is attainable, but conceptual knowledge is treated as limited — liberating knowledge is non-discursive.
Experience and practice first; the Buddha as teacher-exemplar, not god. Traditional forms weigh canon and lineage heavily; the secular form explicitly demotes both.
Phenomenological and anti-essentialist: categories and the self are dependently originated constructions; the emphasis is on how experience arises rather than on a view-from-nowhere.
Restraint of craving and right livelihood cut against consumption- and acceleration-driven cultures, without an explicit technology doctrine.
High in the ethical-contemplative domain: intentions and training reshape experience (karma as intention); conditioned processes can be retrained — a middle path between determinism and randomness.
Objective-leaning but grounded in the structure of suffering rather than commands: non-harming and compassion; karma as moral causation (psychological in the secular reading).
Secular reading: naturalist or agnostic, non-theist, mind studied phenomenologically. (Traditional Buddhism affirms rebirth and multiple world-realms.)
Impermanence is fundamental and clinging to fixed forms is the root error — accepting of change, without a program of social dynamism.
Non-harming and interdependence: humans within the web of conditioned existence, not its masters.
The path's telos — release from suffering, wisdom, compassion — is given by the structure of experience, realized through personal practice.
Interdependence and sangha (practice community) balance the individual path.
